solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Launch punch immediately before being grabbed

indicators.note: the second phrase is held inside the first, as if grabbed by the punch

parts.note: boff is a chiefly North American word for a hit or punch
last means immediately preceding, as in last week

explanation.surface: A boxer launches a punch the instant before an opponent grabs hold in a clinch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket's launch is its moment of lift-off, the countdown's final event.

clue.text: Sensational blonde had rotund bum

indicators.note: bum means bad or worthless, so the letters are a bad arrangement to be reworked

explanation.surface: Tabloid gossip: a fair-haired person with a round behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like the noun for bottom, but as an adjective meaning poor it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood-and-thunder describes melodramatic, violent fiction or rhetoric, full of lurid sensation.

clue.text: Some Sloane Rangers going round O2, for example

indicators.note: going round means that run is read in the opposite direction
some of the letters of the two words are taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Posh young Londoners heading out to a concert at the O2.
explanation.walkthrough: Sloane Rangers are wealthy young people from London's Chelsea area; the O2 is a big London concert venue.
explanation.definitionFit: The O2 in Greenwich is a large indoor venue for concerts and sport.

clue.text: Base one legend on brief madness

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: read as leg end, the end of a leg is a toe

indicators.note: brief means the madness word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: rage is a fit of fury or madness

explanation.surface: A tall story built on a short spell of insanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legend' splits as leg-end. Toerag is British slang for a contemptible person.
explanation.definitionFit: A low, despicable person is a base one, a scoundrel or scumbag in British slang.

clue.text: Using which gear changes can be effected

definitions.text: Using which gear changes can be effected

parts.words: Using which gear changes can be effected
parts.note: gear also means clothing, so changes of outfit happen in these shop cubicles

explanation.surface: A motoring description of a gearbox mechanism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' looks mechanical, but it means clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops provide small cubicles where customers try on and change clothes.

clue.text: Runs out of worn copper parts, causing malfunctions

indicators.note: worn suggests something battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: CU is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: the runs letter leaves the word parts, as something taken out of it

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A machine keeps stopping because its worn copper components have run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn' is the anagram signal: PARTS loses R ('Runs out of') to give PATS, and CU plus PATS is shuffled. 'causing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to behave badly or fail to work properly, so a faulty machine acts up.

clue.text: Short flute composition that could be deep and rich

definitions.text: that could be deep and rich

indicators.note: short means both words lose their final letter

parts.note: to flute is to make ridges, the same as crimp
a song is a musical composition

explanation.surface: A brief piece of flute music that might sound deep and rich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flute' and 'composition' look musical, but flute here means to make ridges. 'Short' cuts both words: CRIMP and SONG lose their final P and G.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a strong, dark red, the kind of colour described as deep and rich.

clue.text: Crack troops who aim to spread the word?

definitions.text: who aim to spread the word?

parts.note: a sally is a witty remark, a crack
an army is a body of troops

explanation.surface: Elite soldiers sent out to spread propaganda.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally Army is a British nickname for the Salvation Army, the Christian church and charity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Salvation Army is an evangelical Christian movement whose members preach the gospel.

clue.text: Primate put mark under trunk on locker

indicators.note: in a down clue, under puts the mark letter below the trunk

parts.note: an elephant's trunk is its proboscis
M is short for mark, the old German currency
a key is what locks something

explanation.surface: An ape is told to stick a label under the tree trunk and on the locker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is taken as it stands; 'trunk' is an elephant's, not a tree's. 'put' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The proboscis monkey of Borneo is a primate known for the male's huge nose.

clue.text: Lightly scored work?

parts.note: a light opera is a musical work written in a light style; 'scored' also suggests marks barely scratched into something

explanation.surface: Something with faint scratches on it, or a job given low marks.
explanation.definitionFit: A short light opera is a musical piece in a comic, tuneful style, so it is lightly scored.

clue.text: Black compound formed by iron crust turning yellow on the inside

indicators.note: turning means those outer letters of iron are read backwards
the crust of iron is its outer shell, its first and last letters
only the inner letters of yellow are taken, its ends dropped

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: heating iron makes a black compound while its crust turns yellow inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron' tempts as the chemical symbol FE, but here the word itself is used: 'crust' is its shell and 'turning' reverses it. 'formed by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Niello is a black metallic alloy of sulphur with silver, copper or lead, used to fill engraved metalwork.

clue.text: Away on account of attraction, returning after this

parts.note: hence, as an old command, means go away
for means because of, on account of

indicators.note: returning means the attraction word is read backwards

parts.note: a draw is something that attracts crowds

explanation.surface: Leaving because of a romantic attraction, then coming back afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Henceforward means from this time on, in future.

clue.text: It's a dream — peppered ham

indicators.note: peppered suggests letters scattered about like seasoning, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dreams of peppered ham and insists it was just a dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ham' looks like the meat but is a verb: to ham is to overact. The apostrophe in It's is no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham it up is to overact, exaggerating a scene for effect, which is what a showy performer does.

clue.text: Scrawny busybody regularly put out a rumour

indicators.note: every third letter of the two words is put out, picked at a steady interval

explanation.surface: A thin, nosy neighbour keeps spreading gossip around the street.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters taken are every third one, starting with the first: S, A, Y, S, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A say-so can be mere hearsay, someone's unsupported word passed along like gossip.

clue.text: Rob perhaps cut off collar

definitions.meaning: a small notch or snip taken off something
to collar a suspect is to arrest them

explanation.surface: Rob, perhaps, has a frayed collar cut off his shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rob' reads as a man's name, but it is the verb to steal. Three meanings sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the same word for steal and arrest, and it also means a small notch.

clue.text: Make bed spanning round short poles

indicators.note: spanning means the bed's letters stretch across the rest, enclosing them

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: round means the short and poles letters are turned the other way

parts.note: curt means brief, short
S and N are the south and north poles

explanation.surface: Instructions to make a bed that stretches around some short poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns CURTSN into NSTRUC, which goes inside COT.
explanation.definitionFit: To construct something is to build or make it.

clue.text: Say nothing about stupid cretin, the selfish one

parts.note: eg, for example, stands in for say
O looks like the figure zero, nothing
C is short for circa, about

indicators.note: stupid suggests muddled thinking, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone stays silent about a foolish person who only thinks of himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-centred person thinks only of themselves; the adjective is also used as a noun for such a person.

clue.text: Note system of actions loony left introduced

indicators.note: the left letter is brought into the middle of the jumbled letters
loony means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of a mad leftist's system of activities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loony' rearranges OF ACTIONS into TONICSOFA; 'introduced' puts L inside, before FA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic sol-fa is a method of teaching singing that names the notes doh, ray, me and so on.

clue.text: I will also be widely received

definitions.meaning: the letter I is the physics symbol for an electric flow, as in V = IR
generally accepted or in common use, as of an idea or word

explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker, but it is the electrical symbol; 'will also be' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A current word or view is one in general circulation, widely accepted right now.

clue.text: Bowled very well, despite these?

parts.note: in cricket, extras given away when the ball beats batsman and wicketkeeper are not counted against the bowler

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator praises a bowler whose figures were good despite some extras conceded.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs scored when the ball passes both batsman and wicketkeeper untouched are extras that do not count against the bowler's figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Byes are runs a team gets without the bat touching the ball, so a bowler can concede them yet still bowl well.

clue.text: Borders of Great Britain toured during control

indicators.note: to tour is to go round, so the border letters go around the next piece
the borders of Great Britain are its outside letters, first and last

parts.note: over means during, as in over the weekend

explanation.surface: The borders of Great Britain were toured while the country was under control.
explanation.definitionFit: To govern is to rule or control a country or people.

clue.text: Absolute maniac losing his head

indicators.note: the first letter of the slang word is dropped, as if beheaded

parts.note: nutter is British slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: A madman is decapitated, as in a grisly tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter means complete or total, as in utter nonsense, an absolute disaster.

clue.text: Traveller's old stuff returned by car

indicators.note: returned means the old and stuff letters are read backwards

parts.note: to cram is to stuff full
the Polo is a Volkswagen car model

explanation.surface: A traveller's old belongings are sent back by car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns OCRAM into MARCO; the 's is 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the Venetian merchant who journeyed across Asia to China in the 13th century.

clue.text: Strokes caused by strobe lighting in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Seizures brought on by flashing strobe lights at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'caused', but strokes alone define the answer; 'caused by' is the link to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are marks such as the dagger or division sign used by scribes to flag dubious passages.

clue.text: Crudely painted plot follows exposed odd man out

indicators.note: follows puts the plot letters after the others
exposed means stripped of outer layers, so each word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot for plants

explanation.surface: An amateur painter's crude canvas, with a plot about a misfit who has been unmasked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd man out' looks like a phrase meaning misfit, but each word is stripped to its middle letter, D, A and U.
explanation.definitionFit: To daub is to smear paint on roughly, so a crudely painted surface has been daubed.

clue.text: Strip then flatten outdated equipment

parts.note: a tape is a narrow strip of material
to deck someone is to knock them flat

explanation.surface: Stripping and flattening some obsolete gear for scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette player is old audio kit, largely replaced by digital music devices.

clue.text: Adelphi's principal has to stop mostly dreadful turn

indicators.note: the first letter goes in to plug a gap, as a stopper fills a hole
mostly means the last letter of the dreadful word is dropped

parts.note: rotten means very bad, dreadful

indicators.note: the principal, or first, letter of Adelphi is used

explanation.surface: The head of the Adelphi theatre has to halt a dreadful variety act.
explanation.walkthrough: The Adelphi is a London West End theatre, so 'turn' reads as a stage act.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn round and round on an axis is to rotate, like a wheel.

clue.text: Character's name altered by a single stroke?

indicators.note: one letter changes into another by moving a single pen stroke: the lower bar of an F shifts up to make a T

parts.note: to identify someone is to name them

explanation.surface: Someone's name has been changed with one stroke of the pen.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital letter F becomes T by changing a single stroke. The 's is 'is', a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Identity is who someone is, their individual character and sense of self.
